posts.text: Attorney General Todd Blanche and the Justice department filed an addendum to the settlement between Donald Trump in the IRS that prevents the IRS and other agencies from continuing any audit or investigation or even starting no investigations against Trump, his family, and his company. The addendum was filed as part of the settlement for the $10 billion lawsuit that Trump filed against the IRS and includes the creation of a $1.7 billion “justice fund“

President Donald Trump has reportedly ended his $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS but is apparently tying that decision to the creation of a $1.7 billion “truth and justice fund” that will be accessible to people who feel they have been unjustly prosecuted by the DOJ and the FBI.

Texas governor Greg Abbott asked the Texas Supreme Court to expel the democratic house members who walked out to prevent a vote on the redrawn congressional district maps. The state Supreme Court rejected his request, the siding that any expulsion would need to come directly from a house vote

The White House just published a document that outlines national security priorities for the U.S. government.  It contains new categories of focus that should concern Americans, because it could make dissent and exercise of the first amendment more difficult

Speaker of the House Mike Johnson suggested that members of the U.S. Congress should be allowed to buy and sell stock because their salary hasn’t changed since 2009 and they need to “take care of their families”.  That’s called insider trading: lawmakers create the policies that affect how the companies whose stock they trade perform.
